findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: "point at a dead port" (the item's own suggested live method for exit 23, and by extension the mechanism the run used to explain exit 18) causes a settings command to fail with SettingsServerUnavailable (18) rather than SettingsServerError (23).
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: A genuinely dead/unbound explicit port (nothing listening, confirmed via lsof before dialing) does NOT produce any error at all -- CliSettingsBackend.AcquireAsync always reuses-or-auto-starts a backend on that port (BackendLauncher[633] 'starting the backend on port N'), and the command completes with exit 0. Exit 18 is produced by a different mechanism entirely: dialing a port already occupied by another data-root's live server, where the token file for your data-root doesn't match the one that server expects.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: Two independent dead-port trials (ports 58421, 58433) both auto-started cleanly, exit 0, confirmed via lsof before and ps/log after. One incidental collision with the machine's own live 7721 server (from omitting --port) produced exit 18 with the exact message 'the backend at http://127.0.0.1:7721/mcp is listening but .../mcp-token holds no token -- a serve on another data root may own port 7721'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: A future lane following the item's literal suggested method ('point at a dead port') on any non-7721 port will get exit 0, not 18 or 23. Exit 18 specifically requires colliding with another data-root's OCCUPIED port -- which lanes must never deliberately do to port 7721 anyway. Does not change either run's pass/substituted verdict; the prior run's reasoning for why 18 (not 23) resulted was about the wrong mechanism.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: docs/work/checklist/2026-08-22-1.31.0-full-product.json, item 'code-model-activation-and-refusal' (and its own PR #453's evidence section)
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The 1.31.0 run's own corrected verdict, and PR #453's own PR-body evidence, both treat 'downloaded faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1@main to <dir> ... code embedding engine set to local (<dir>); the code-reindex maintenance job will re-embed pending rows' as proof the default code model now works end-to-end (#422 resolved).

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: This same file, this same run (docs/work/checklist/2026-08-22-1.32.0-post-delta-wave.json), items 'code-model-one-command-install' / 'code-search-discriminates-on-engine-activation' / 'doctor-reports-active-code-model', as originally filed against build dc1747d7419feb9457122c71b07eda93b74da00a
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The first pass of this same run recorded a STOP-and-report regression: the code-reindex job silently exhausted MaxEmbedAttempts=3 without ever embedding a row, and kind=code search returned a hard 'code-engine-unloadable: ... Specified argument was out of the range of valid values' error against the real, correctly-downloaded faxenoff/code-daemon-embed-v1 model.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The root cause was traced and fixed by PR #466/#467 ('pool by the ONNX output's rank, not the manifest's guess'): the manifest declares pooling.mode='cls', but the model's own ONNX graph already pools internally (output 'last_hidden_state' is [batch, dimensions], not [batch, seq_len, dimensions]), so applying a second, manifest-directed CLS-token extraction on top indexed out of range. The fix pools by the graph output's actual rank instead of trusting the manifest's declared mode, and logs an informational warning when the two disagree (observed live in this re-test) rather than crashing.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: Re-run against merged HEAD 62bf49b0ddba40b1102491722a6107c791dc173c (PR #464 + PR #467 merged): code_entries.embed_state='embedded', embed_attempts=0 on two independent scratch roots (Python and TypeScript fixtures); doctor reports pending:0 on both; kind=code search returns a real hit with no error and no warning; a literal-overlap control confirms the vector leg's ranking genuinely responds to query content.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: This run's own earlier verdict (fail/not-accepted on both items) is superseded, not wrong -- it correctly caught a real regression that has now been fixed in the same PR cycle. A future run should not re-flag 'code-engine-unloadable' against this exact repo/manifest pairing as a new discovery; it should check whether PR #467's pooling-by-rank logic is still in place first. This run also surfaced a secondary, lower-severity observation while re-verifying (recorded in 'code-search-discriminates-on-engine-activation's acceptance-reason): semantic ranking between two short, register-mismatched code snippets did not perfectly discriminate by topic in a 2-document toy corpus -- worth a dedicated item with a larger, better-controlled fixture set in a future run, not a blocker for this release.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: ai-raccoon model set local (bundled ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2, activated before writing) ; wrote 4 entries (sextant target + JWT/auth, password-reset, decision distractors) ; confirmed embed_state=embedded (1536-byte/384-dim blobs) via ?mode=ro before searching ; memory_search default weights, query='an old-fashioned tool sailors used to gauge their position by watching the stars from the deck at night' (zero literal overlap with the sextant text) ; same query with ftsWeight=0/vectorWeight=1 and with ftsWeight=1/vectorWeight=0 to isolate each leg ; memory_search query='reset your password account settings security' (literal-overlap control)
items.evidence:
Default hybrid (1:1) -> ranked: JWT/auth (1.0), sextant (0.984), password-reset (0.968), decision (0.953) -- sextant present at rank 2, not rank 1.
Vector-only (ftsWeight=0) -> sextant (1.0) rank 1, JWT (0.984), decision (0.968), password-reset (0.953) -- confirms the semantic leg alone puts the target first.
FTS-only (vectorWeight=0) -> JWT (1.0) rank 1, password-reset (0.984), sextant (0.968), decision (0.953) -- FTS5's documented OR-fallback (no AND match, so it falls back to an OR of every content token) matches every doc on some stray token and produces this near-arbitrary order in a 4-doc corpus.
Literal-overlap control -> password-reset ranks 1 (1.0), reordering correctly vs. the semantic query.
items.observed-result: The entry IS returned through hybrid search (rank 2 of 4, well inside default minRelativeScore=0), and isolating the two legs proves both are functioning: the vector leg alone puts the zero-overlap target at rank 1, and the FTS leg alone (via the documented OR-fallback for an under-matching query) is what pulls the unrelated JWT entry ahead of it under default 1:1 weights in this small corpus. The literal-overlap control confirms ranking is query-sensitive, not fixed.
items.acceptance-reason: The item's contract (memory_search retrieves the entry through hybrid RRF) is met and verified live; the counter-intuitive rank-2 result under default weights is explained and reproduced deliberately by isolating each leg, not hand-waved -- it is FTS5's documented OR-fallback behavior in a small corpus, not a broken vector leg.
